r.rootCauseOneLine: bb keeps one long-lived `claude` CLI process per thread (never recycled after a rate-limit/auth failure), and that process memoizes the OAuth token it loaded at startup, only invalidating it when the mtime of ~/.claude/.credentials.json changes or via a 30 s (stale-on-failure) Keychain cache on macOS; a login the probe cannot see stays pinned until a new process (server restart / thread stop) is spawned.
r.proposedFix: In plugins/provider-claude-code/src/bridge/bridge.ts, when a turn's SDK result is_error with category rate-limit/unauthorized/billing (error-info.ts), flag the ThreadSession recycle-on-next-input and have getWritableThreadSession treat it like streamEnded: settle, emitSessionReplacement, and start(providerThreadId) a fresh SDK session (existing replaceEndedThreadSession path). The new claude process reads credentials at startup so a login done in between applies on retry; conversation survives via SDK resume; no wire change (no protocol bump). Interim workaround: `bb thread stop <id>` on the idle thread releases the runtime so the next message spawns a fresh process (verified).
r.caveats: Plain Linux flow (claude login rewrites .credentials.json) does NOT reproduce with Claude Code 2.1.233/2.1.234: the CLI notices the mtime change and reloads on the next request. The pinned-token behaviour was reproduced deterministically only when the store changes without an mtime change (Linux analog of a macOS Keychain login next to a leftover plaintext file, or a failed/timed-out Keychain re-read). macOS could not be run here; the Keychain-cache analysis comes from reading the shipped darwin binaries' embedded JS. Reporter's OS/CLI version unknown; suggested check: `ls -la ~/.claude/.credentials.json` on their Mac and CLI debug logs for "[keychain] read failed; serving stale cache".

r.rootCauseOneLine: Three of the 11 listed surfaces really map unbounded/huge arrays into small scroll boxes (CSV preview mounts all 50,000 td of its 500x100 cap; prompt-banner WorkspaceChangesList mounts one row per changed file even while collapsed and the status payload is unbounded; RemotePathBrowser renders every readdir entry); the other 8 are bounded upstream, tiny in practice, an unused container, or a misread of the pagination helper.
r.proposedFix: (1) Virtualize CSV preview tbody rows (and optionally columns) with the already-used @tanstack/react-virtual over the existing scroll container, keeping sticky thead; interim content-visibility:auto on tr helps layout but not memory. (2) In ThreadPromptContextBanner, don't mount the git body while collapsed and pass `limit` to WorkspaceChangesList (metadata panel already does) or virtualize; additionally cap WorkspaceStatus.workingTree.files at the daemon boundary with maxFiles/truncated like WORKSPACE_DIFF_MAX_FILES (protocol version bump). (3) Add a limit/truncated pair to the daemon directory-listing command used by RemotePathBrowser (protocol version bump) and virtualize the h-56 list. Leave small-data surfaces alone; close command.tsx and resource-pagination.tsx entries as false positives.
r.caveats: No iOS device/simulator available; measurements are headless Chromium 145 (dev build and a production `vite preview` build) with 1x and 4x CPU throttling as a phone stand-in. Worktree HEAD was a108fa7ef (5 commits past base); I checked out 16ceb3a54 for all work; nothing on origin/main since fixes this. The repro vitest file passes on main (documents current behavior) rather than failing. `dev-browser --browser bb1615 stop` stopped the shared dev-browser daemon (other agents' named pages may have been closed; the daemon auto-restarts on next use).

r.rootCauseOneLine: ThreadDetailView mounts ~12-15 independent per-thread queries with nothing deferred, and useEnvironmentWorkStatus (staleTime 0, refetchOnMount "always") / useEnvironmentPullRequest (refetchOnMount, refetchOnWindowFocus "always") drive uncached server->daemon git and `gh pr view` probes (70-260 ms git, 1.1-1.6 s GitHub API) on every open, forming a 3-tier waterfall.
r.proposedFix: (1) Cache workspace.status in the host daemon per environment, invalidated by the existing WatchManager work-status-changed/git-refs-changed events and daemon-owned mutations, with a short TTL and coalescing (daemon-internal, no protocol bump). (2) Stop probing GitHub per open: useEnvironmentPullRequest -> refetchOnMount false, drop refetchOnWindowFocus "always", refresh on git-refs-changed only, and memoize the last gh pr view result per branch in the daemon. (3) Gate status/PR queries, thread-storage listing, tabs, and fork/parent child-thread lists on the surface that renders them being open (none visible on mobile first paint). (4) Fix the double status refetch per open. Do not add an aggregate bootstrap endpoint (rejected history in #335/#1470/#1481).
r.caveats: Measured in dev mode (Vite, StrictMode double-fires, HTTP/1.1 proxy) with a 1-message thread; distinct-URL counts (12-15) are slightly below the issue's ~19 and depend on the thread's tabs/panels. Mobile RTT was emulated via CDP in headless Chromium, not a real iPhone; the reporter's 3-15 s taps over a Cloudflare tunnel were not reproduced on-device. The pull-request timing used a scratch repo pointed at github.com/get-bb/bb (gh returns absent after a real API call). The dev-browser sandbox could not apply throttling, so the throttled run uses a plain-node Playwright script.

r.rootCauseOneLine: status-changed realtime pushes carry no row data and the app's registry rule for them invalidates the single monolithic sidebarNavigation query (full ThreadListEntry for every visible thread of every project, ~1 KB/row) with an immediate flush, so every turn start/end re-downloads the whole 134 KB bootstrap instead of patching one row.
r.proposedFix: (1) Add optional status/runtime to threadChangeMetadataSchema, have every notifyThread(["status-changed"]) caller include the post-transition values, and change the app's status-changed rule to patch the row in the thread-list and sidebar caches (mirroring the existing hasPendingInteraction patch path), falling back to the current dirtyThreadListQueries only when metadata is missing or the row is not cached; server<->app only, no daemon protocol bump. (2) Introduce a trimmed sidebarThreadEntrySchema for sidebar-bootstrap threads and drop per-project sources/defaultExecutionOptions from the bootstrap. (3) Optionally scope remaining refetches per project (per-project query keys or ?projectId= on the route) and give status-changed the 50 ms debounce once it is a cache patch.
r.caveats: Measured on the Vite dev build (React dev runtime), so absolute CPU numbers are inflated; ratios and byte counts are what matter. JSON parse and whole-tree re-render claims in the issue are overstated (parse ~1 ms at 6x throttle; structural sharing keeps unchanged rows), the real per-event cost is wire bytes + one server-side full list read + O(all threads) deep-compare. The 650-930 ms render on idle->active is the active-row reorder and would occur with a patch too. Side finding: pnpm seed:perf fails with a FOREIGN KEY error if the dev server is running (destroyed-environment prune races the seed); it must be run with the server stopped. Worktree HEAD was a108fa7ef on start; I checked out 16ceb3a54 for all measurements.

r.rootCauseOneLine: All SQLite reads are synchronous on the single server event loop; the original 11 s thread-list stall (listLatestGoalEventRowsByThreadIds) was fixed by #1204, but the latest timeline page still runs two window-independent whole-thread scans (listTodoSnapshotEventRowsForThread fetching every tool-call payload, and listStoredEventRowsByParentToolCallIds with sequenceBounds=null walking every event with json_extract), reading ~100 MB / 918 major faults for a 1.7 MiB page on a 44k-event thread and blocking every other request for the duration.
r.proposedFix: 1) Bound the parent/child backfill on the latest page: pass sequenceStart: window.sequenceStart instead of sequenceBounds null in selectStandardTimelineEventRows (apps/server/src/services/threads/timeline.ts ~L1450) and back listStoredEventRowsByParentToolCallIds with a partial index on rows that have a parentToolCallId, so it stops walking all 44k events with json_extract. 2) Make listTodoSnapshotEventRowsForThread index-only: add a partial expression index events(thread_id, sequence) WHERE item_kind='toolCall' AND type IN ('item/started','item/completed') AND json_extract(data,'$.item.tool') IN ('TodoWrite','TaskCreate','TaskUpdate','TaskList','TaskGet') via Drizzle migration, spell the predicate literally and pin with INDEXED BY (verified on the seeded db: plan becomes SEARCH USING INDEX events_todo_snapshot_idx (thread_id=?), 520 rows instead of every tool-call payload) plus a query-plan regression test; or persist the todo snapshot as thread state. 3) Re-measure cold with the profiler; only then consider the shared DB-layer read worker from #1207. 4) Separately lower COMPLETED_EVENT_OUTPUT_TRUNCATION_THRESHOLD_CHARS (32 KB) toward 4-8 KB; the 250 batch is a per-10 s scan limit, not the constraint.
r.caveats: Absolute stall times were reproduced at ~10x smaller magnitude (0.3-0.46 s cold vs the reporter's 3.4 s) because this host has local NVMe and 16 cores; the transferable evidence is 99.7 MB of disk reads / 918 major page faults for a 1.7 MiB page and the query plans, not milliseconds. I could not throttle IOPS without root. The seeded thread is codex-shaped (70 MB) rather than the reporter's 131 MiB; a claude-code thread with large toolCall results would make the todo scan proportionally worse. That these two scans were exactly what dominated the reporter's 0.37.0 measurement is inferred from the profile shape (medium confidence); the loop-blocking mechanism itself is high confidence. The unit test documents current plans and passes on main (not a failing repro). No screenshots (not a visual bug).

r.rootCauseOneLine: bb-app's native add-ons (better-sqlite3, node-pty) are only built by npm install scripts; npm 11's allowScripts policy is advisory (scripts still run, so the reporter's npm 11.17 mechanism is refuted), but npm 12 (registry latest since 2026-07-08) blocks unreviewed dependency scripts by default and, for -g/npx installs, ignores the package's own allowScripts, so every bb install path (npm -g, npx, install.sh, daemon self-update) that passes no --allow-scripts yields a bb that crashes with "Could not locate the bindings file" / "Failed to load native module: pty.node"; the PATH sub-issue was already fixed by #1419.
r.proposedFix: Add --allow-scripts=better-sqlite3,node-pty,@parcel/watcher to both `npm install -g` lines in apps/server/src/assets/install-machine.sh and to the self-updater argv in apps/host-daemon/src/protocol-self-update.ts (defaultInstallTarball); verified end to end that this makes the npm 12.0.2 machine join succeed, that npm 11 accepts the flag and npm 10.9.9 ignores it. After npm install, verify `require(better-sqlite3)`/`require(node-pty)` load and fail the installer loudly with a pointer to --allow-scripts / ignore-scripts (diff in 1120/repro/1120-installer-fix.diff; requires updating the fake npm and argv regexes in apps/server/test/app/install-machine-script.test.ts). Document `npx --allow-scripts=better-sqlite3,node-pty,@parcel/watcher bb-app@latest` (or `npm config set allow-scripts=... --location=user`) in the README quick start/troubleshooting and packages/bb-app/README.md. Longer term, node:sqlite removes better-sqlite3 from the list. No wire changes, no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.
r.caveats: The reporter's own breakage on npm 11.17.0 could not be reproduced (npm 11.16/11.17 run the scripts and bb starts; the maintainer found the same); the reporter never posted the actual error, so their root cause is unverified. The reproduced failure requires npm 12.0.x, which is registry `latest` but not yet bundled with any released Node (Node 24.19 ships 11.17.0, Node 26.7 ships 11.19.0). Tested on Linux only; the macOS installer path was checked by code reading (#1419 removed the PATH check). Tests used bb-app@latest = 0.38.0 from the registry plus the base-commit tarball served by my dev server, not 0.35.1. Once a CLI policy is passed, npm 12 skips all other unlisted scripts (currently only @google/genai's no-op preinstall and protobufjs's postinstall; bb ran fine without them).

r.rootCauseOneLine: apps/app/src/components/ui/markdown-code-highlight.ts maps only rust/python/go/c/java/css fence languages to sugar-high v1 presets; sh/bash/shell/zsh/console (and yaml, toml, sql, diff, ...) get preset=undefined and fall through to sugar-high's JavaScript lexer, so `#` is a sign, words are identifiers, and `/plugins/monokai` is a regex-literal string.
r.proposedFix: Preferred: bump apps/app sugar-high to ^2.0.1 and in markdown-code-highlight.ts replace the preset map with `import { lang } from "sugar-high/lang"` -> `highlight(code, { lang: lang(language) ?? EXTRA_ALIASES[language] })`, with EXTRA_ALIASES covering h/hpp->c(pp), less->css, console->shell (verified: lang() maps sh/bash/zsh/shell->shell and 25 langs incl. yaml/toml/sql/diff/json; HTML still uses sh__token--* / --sh-* so the CSS is untouched; only this file imports sugar-high). Alternative minimal v1 patch: add a local shell preset (python-style `#` comment handlers + shell keywords) mapped from sh/bash/shell/zsh/console and wire the shipped `diff` preset; fixes comments but v1's regex-literal heuristic still paints unquoted paths like ./plugins/monokai as strings.
r.caveats: No linked PR to review (PR #1317 is a Streamdown PoC referenced only as evidence). Minor issue inaccuracy: sugar-high 1.2.1 ships seven presets (no json), not eight. Screenshots are light theme only. Worktree was moved to base 16ceb3a54 (HEAD was origin/main a108fa7ef, which does not touch the relevant files, so not fixed upstream). r.rootCauseOneLine: codex app-server replays the previous turn's token usage on thread/resume and thread/fork; the codex bridge stamps that old Codex turn id with the NEW session's per-session prefix (bt<entropy>-<serial>-), so the server sees a turn it never stored turn/started for and (by design) drops the snapshot with a warn log — on resume the payload is an exact duplicate of what is already stored (log noise only), on fork the parent's inherited context usage is discarded until the fork's first turn.
r.proposedFix: Keep the server-side orphan drop (it is the correct safety net; buffering would re-create the fork batch-wedging bug). Fix in the codex bridge (plugins/provider-codex/src/bridge/bridge.ts, toCanonicalEvents ~L620): track Codex turn ids this session has emitted turn/started for; for thread/tokenUsage/updated or thread/contextWindowUsage/updated naming any other turn (only resume/fork replays do that), emit the context-window usage thread-scoped ({kind:"thread"} is allowed by the domain scope policy and is what the ACP bridge already does) and drop the token usage (turn-only by policy; duplicate of the persisted snapshot on resume, parent's cumulative total on fork). Prototype diff in the artifacts typechecks and keeps the full codex plugin suite green (165 passed). Optionally add scope.turnId to the server warn line and lower it to info/debug. No wire changes, no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.
r.caveats: Not a visual bug, so no screenshots. The worktree was created at a108fa7ef (origin/main tip) rather than 16ceb3a54; I checked out 16ceb3a54 before the live runs and rebuilt (relevant files are equivalent between the two). The bridge-level repro test needs a small opt-in extension of the test fixture fake-codex-app-server.mjs (diff included) to mirror the real app-server's usage replay on resume; the real behavior is proven separately by the raw codex app-server probe and the live bb runs. Server-log instrumentation (adds scope/data to the warn line) was applied for the second live run only to show which turn id was dropped; the warning itself reproduces without it. Live runs consumed a handful of tiny codex turns ("Reply only with ok.").

r.rootCauseOneLine: plugins/provider-acp/src/interactions.ts buildAcpPermissionInteractionPayload always emits a `command` approval subject with command = rawInput.command ?? title ?? kind, ignoring the ACP toolCall.kind ("edit") and locations, so a file-write permission (no rawInput.command, title = file/dir path) renders as "run this command $ /path" and the server materialises it as a commandExecution timeline item under the same toolCallId that event-translation already/next emits as fileChange.
r.proposedFix: In plugins/provider-acp: forward toolCall.locations[].path from handlePermissionRequest (bridge.ts) into AcpPermissionToolCall, and in buildAcpPermissionInteractionPayload (interactions.ts) return a `file_change` subject {itemId: toolCallId, writeScope: first location ?? null, sessionGrant: null} when toolCall.kind is edit/delete/move and no rawInput.command is present; keep the command fallback otherwise. No server/protocol change (file_change is already a legal subject; wire shape unchanged, so no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump). Patch at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1719/repro/proposed-fix.patch; verified: repro test passes, existing interactions/bridge tests (75) pass, typecheck passes, app shows "Do you want to make these changes?" and timeline stays fileChange. Open choice: writeScope as file path vs dirname vs null (UI labels it "Write root").
r.caveats: opencode is not installed on this machine, so the live repro uses bb's fake ACP agent extended to emit exactly what opencode's ACP layer sends for a write permission (kind "edit", title = path, locations, rawInput without command), registered via customAcpAgents; the opencode-side shapes were verified from anomalyco/opencode source (acp/permission.ts, acp/tool.ts). Whether the reporter's "bare directory" came from opencode's write permission (title = file path) or external_directory permission (title = parentDir) is unverified; both hit the same code path. The worktree was left with the proposed fix applied plus the repro test (uncommitted); worktree HEAD is detached at 16ceb3a54 (it started at a108fa7ef). Not fixed on origin/main as of a108fa7ef.

r.rootCauseOneLine: buildTimelineTurnSummaryDetails drops every turn-scoped row whose turnId differs from the requested turn (filterExactEventRowsForRequestedTurn), so a late item/completed scoped to the next turn is discarded and neither the scoped-identity whole-item closure (#1510) nor any backfill restores it, while the timeline projection merges the same lifecycle by bare call id (#447) — details render the call unfinished (pending, or interrupted on an idle thread) with no output.
r.proposedFix: In apps/server/src/services/threads/timeline.ts filterExactEventRowsForRequestedTurn, track item ids that the requested turn item/started inside the window and keep another turn's non-backgroundTask item/* rows for those ids, dropping ownership if another turn emits its own item/started for the same id (preserves #1398 id-reuse isolation). Prototype patch (1714/repro/prototype-fix.patch) makes the invariant test (details.rows toEqual inline children) pass and keeps the other 115 apps/server thread tests green. Before shipping: also fetch the completion when it lies beyond sourceSeqEnd (byte-cut turns) and reconcile the exact-bounds match so it does not turn into a missing-match 500; add the invariant test next to #1510's in timeline-in-turn-window.test.ts. Server-only, no protocol bump.
r.caveats: Did not provoke a real late tool_result from a live provider; the persisted event shape was seeded directly (unit test with in-memory SQLite, and @bb/db insert into the dev instance DB) — that shape is exactly what the claude-code translator emits per code reading. Correction to the issue: on a real idle thread the wrong details row reads 'interrupted' / 'Tool execution interrupted' rather than 'pending' (pending only while thread status is starting/active). The issue's file path for the translator (packages/agent-runtime/src/shared/tool-item-translation.ts) does not exist at base; the equivalent lives in packages/provider-bridge-protocol/src/bridge-kit/tool-item-translation.ts. Bug also present on origin/main a108fa7ef. Worktree left with three untracked test/seed files under apps/server/test/services/threads/ (no source changes).

r.rootCauseOneLine: bb stores and serves pasted HEIC bytes verbatim as a localImage (content-type image/heic) and renders the URL in a plain ; Chromium (web + Electron) has no HEIC decoder and bb never transcodes, so the thumbnail/timeline image is broken — and the provider (Codex) cannot process the image either.
r.proposedFix: Transcode HEIC/HEIF once at the server upload boundary in storeAttachment (apps/server/src/services/projects/attachments.ts): detect image/heic|heif (or .heic/.heif extension), decode with a WASM libheif package (heic-decode/heic-convert; sharp's prebuilt libvips lacks HEIC), store JPEG (PNG if alpha), return mimeType image/jpeg + new path/sizeBytes, enforce the 10MB limit on output, 400 on decode failure. No wire/protocol change needed. Also render an "unsupported image" tile on onError in AttachmentPreview/ConversationAttachments. Regression test = the repro vitest (upload real HEIC -> served type must be Chromium-decodable).
r.caveats: Repro run on Linux headless Chromium 145 (same Blink decoders as Electron); macOS Safari would likely render HEIC natively (not tested, no Apple hardware). r.rootCauseOneLine: Volta stamps _VOLTA_TOOL_RECURSION=1 on the bb-app it launches; bb forwards it to the daemon and sanitizeInheritedChildProcessEnv (packages/process-utils/src/index.ts:188) only strips BB_*/NODE_ENV, while the daemon swaps PATH for the login-shell PATH that puts Volta's node/npm/npx shims back in front, so the shims see the guard, skip platform resolution and fail with "Node is not available" (also breaking $BB_CLI and bb, both #!/usr/bin/env node).
r.proposedFix: Strip _VOLTA_TOOL_RECURSION in sanitizeInheritedChildProcessEnv (packages/process-utils/src/index.ts), the single choke point for every bb-spawned child (provider bridges, terminals, git, plugin hosts, script automations); one-hunk diff at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1545/repro/proposed-fix.diff. Mirrors Volta's own `volta run` (removes the same var because a new command is a new context). No wire change, no protocol bump. Verified: repro test flips from fail to pass and the same Claude Code turn prints v24.19.0 while the daemon still carries the guard. Optional hardening: also drop it in bb-app createDaemonEnv/createServerEnv.
r.caveats: Reproduced on Linux with Volta 2.0.2 installed into a scratch VOLTA_HOME and a wrapper $SHELL so the daemon's login-shell PATH probe yields "Volta shims first, no other Node" (the reporter's mac/zsh setup is not available). The one simulated element is injecting _VOLTA_TOOL_RECURSION=1 into the dev instance's env instead of launching bb-app through a real Volta package shim; a real Volta package shim (probe package installed via `npm i -g` under Volta) was shown to set exactly that variable. The worktree HEAD had drifted to a108fa7ef at start; I pinned it to 16ceb3a54 before all repro runs (none of the 5 intervening commits touch the relevant files). The worktree now contains the proposed fix and the repro test (uncommitted).

r.rootCauseOneLine: timelineWindowEventBudget bounds synchronous timeline builds by a fixed event count justified by a one-host "0.06ms/event" figure, but build cost is CPU- and payload-byte-dependent (SQLite read + JSON.parse ~80%), so on slow hosts a full 1500-event window blocks the event loop far longer than the ~100ms the constant promises; the existing 4 MiB byte cut is not operator-tunable and never engages for latency.

prReviews.topFinding: Docs-only; bakes one VPS's unverifiable and selection-biased numbers (derived only from >=150ms slow-build log lines) into the shared feature-flags.ts JSDoc, and the configuration.md recipe omits that the log samples only the slow tail and that a whole finished turn is always returned even above the budget; does not touch the real lever (the existing byte-based window cut).

r.proposedFix: Promote the existing THREAD_TIMELINE_EVENT_DATA_BYTE_LIMIT (4 MiB, applyTimelineWindowByteBudget / findStoredTimelineWindowByteBudgetFloor) to a feature flag timelineWindowByteBudget (BB_FF_TIMELINE_WINDOW_BYTE_BUDGET) threaded like eventBudget, default ~1.5 MiB with 4 MiB kept as the memory clamp; document both knobs (configuration.md, guide template, bb-cli skill) and reword the source comment to say the count is a hardware/payload-dependent proxy. Avoid runtime calibration unless the timeline cache and latest-rows keys also include the effective budget. Structural fix (out of scope): incremental projection or moving the build off the event loop.
r.caveats: Could not measure on the reporter's 4-core VPS; hardware dependence was demonstrated by CPU-throttling the same test (~4x cost, 124.5ms > 100ms for a full window) rather than on real slow hardware. On this Ryzen 7 workstation the constant is conservative (0.024 ms/event). The reporter's 0.479 ms/event p50 is a slow-tail estimate because the log line only fires for builds >= 150ms. Nothing on origin/main after the base commit changes this code. No dev instance or provider turns were needed.

findings.section: Root cause / Claims vs findings (cache-key row)
findings.problem: The report states 'the server pays the full-window cost per appended event, back-to-back' and marks 'every appended event invalidates the entry and an active thread rebuilds continuously' as Verified. The cache-key part is true, but the client deliberately paces its trailing refetch to the observed fetch duration (min 50 ms, max 1 s, ~50% duty cycle) and coalesces events that arrive mid-fetch, so builds are NOT once-per-appended-event; PR #882 introduced exactly this pacing. The sustained-rebuild mechanism is real but its magnitude is overstated.
findings.evidence: apps/app/src/hooks/cache-owners/realtime-cache-registry.ts L135-L157 at 16ceb3a54: 'Waiting out the observed build cost caps that duty cycle near 50%'; TRAILING_REFETCH_MIN_INTERVAL_MS = 50, resolveTrailingRefetchDelayMs(observedFetchDurationMs). PR #882 body: 'The client's trailing refetch is paced to the observed build duration.'
findings.fix: Reword the row to 'Verified (cache key) / Partially: the client throttles refetches to ~50% duty cycle, so rebuilds are sustained but coalesced, not one per event' and cite realtime-cache-registry.ts.

findings.problem: The first `it(...)` is titled 'a full 1500-event window builds within the documented ~100ms cold-build target' but never asserts that (only `expect(samples.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`; full-window n=0 in both runs). A reader running vitest sees a passing test whose name promises a check that is not made.
findings.evidence: timeline-event-budget-cost.repro.test.ts L87, L174, output line 'full-window builds (>= 1350 events, n=0)'.
findings.fix: Rename the first scenario to something like 'per-event cost across the perf fixture (informational)'.

findings.section: Root cause — Deeper issue / Related issues
findings.problem: The report presents 'the budget bounds count, not bytes' as its own discovered deeper issue, but PR #882's own 'Known limits' already states 'The budget bounds event count, not bytes' and '1500 is a first guess ... The new logs are how we'll tune it'. Not crediting this makes the calibration gap look unanticipated when the original author flagged it.
findings.evidence: gh pr view 882 body, 'Known limits' section.
findings.fix: Add one sentence in Related issues / Deeper issue noting PR #882 already listed the count-vs-bytes limitation and called 1500 a first guess.

findings.problem: The contended run is a synthetic slowdown whose pass/fail depends on the host: the threshold is 100 ms and measured p50 was 124.5 ms (author) / 141.9 ms (me); on a faster CPU sharing one core with three busy loops it could pass. run-contended.sh also hardcodes CORE=3 and requires `taskset` (Linux only) without saying so in the report body.
findings.evidence: run-contended.sh (CORE=${CORE:-3}, taskset), verify output p50=141.9 vs 124.5.
findings.fix: State the Linux/taskset prerequisite and that the assertion is expected to fail only when the throttled per-event cost exceeds ~0.067 ms; optionally use 4-5 busy loops for margin.

r.rootCauseOneLine: Subscription-mode voice transcription posts to the ChatGPT web app's Cloudflare-bot-protected endpoint https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/transcribe (not a Codex endpoint); when Cloudflare returns a managed challenge (403 + cf-mitigated: challenge) the daemon retries once with cookies, then throws non-transient codex_request_failed carrying the challenge HTML, so the server neither retries nor falls back and the user sees "HTTP 502: Codex transcription request failed with HTTP 403: <html>...".
r.proposedFix: Daemon: in transcribeCodexVoice/createCodexHttpError, when the response is still a Cloudflare challenge after the cookie retry, throw codex_service_unavailable (or a new codex_cloudflare_challenge code added to the server's isTransientInferenceError, with a HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump) with a clean message, and never append text/html bodies to error messages. Server: make the transcription fallback meaningful — if OPENAI_API_KEY is configured, fall back to the openai/<model> path (api.openai.com) after a transient/challenge failure instead of fallbackModel === primary model; otherwise keep one delayed retry; map the final challenge failure to buildTranscriptionUnavailableError() (503) and document that BB_TRANSCRIPTION=openai/... + OPENAI_API_KEY avoids chatgpt.com. Optionally persist Cloudflare cookies across daemon restarts. Key any transient classification on cf-mitigated: challenge only, not on all 403s.
r.caveats: Could not trigger a real Cloudflare challenge from this network with the daemon's full header set (0/18: 8 real daemon calls + 10 curl); the same request with only Authorization was challenged 7/10 and unauthenticated 10/10, so the end-to-end CLI failure was reproduced by injecting the real captured challenge response into the daemon via a Node --import fetch preload (deterministic simulation), plus a unit test that fails on main. Why the reporters' networks are challenged even with the headers is inferred (Cloudflare bot score per IP/fingerprint), not observed. The API-key path was verified by code only (no OpenAI API key available). Worktree HEAD was a108fa7ef (5 commits after base 16ceb3a54); all involved files are byte-identical to the base and permalinks point at the base. No screenshots (CLI/network bug, not visual). Dev instance stopped; worktree contains two uncommitted files (apps/host-daemon/src/codex-chatgpt-client-1587.test.ts, apps/host-daemon/live-probe-1587.ts).

v.reproResult: Followed all five layers (A–E) in my own worktree (HEAD a108fa7ef, involved files identical to base 16ceb3a54; git log 16ceb3a54..origin/main touches none of them, so not fixed on main). A: waf-probe.sh reproduced verbatim — /backend-api/transcribe returns HTTP 403 + cf-mitigated: challenge for all 5 UAs, /backend-api/codex/responses returns 401 (verify/waf-probe.log). B: waf-probe-headers.py gave the identical table (auth+account/originator → 200, auth only → 403 challenge, nothing → 403); waf-sample.py tally full-daemon-headers 10/10 200, authorization-only 9/10 403 (report had 7/10; consistent 'coin flip'). C: live-probe-1587.ts via pnpm exec tsx → 8/8 OK text='...'. D: started my dev instance (server :23860, daemon :31860) with NODE_OPTIONS preload; system/config voiceTranscriptionEnabled:true; baseline CLI run printed '...' exit 0; challenge run printed exactly 'Error: HTTP 502: Codex transcription request failed with HTTP 403: <html> <head> <meta name="viewport" ...' exit=1, preload log shows 2 daemon fetches (original + cookie retry carrying the simulated __cf_bm), daemon log errorCode codex_request_failed, server log 'Voice transcription failed {attempts:1,maxAttempts:2}'; removing the flag file restored transcription. r.rootCauseOneLine: resolveRelativeLocalFileHref (apps/app/src/components/ui/markdown-local-file-link.ts L294-L323) rejects absolute/fragment/query/scheme hrefs but has no case for shell home paths, so `~/x` is string-joined onto the workspace root, yielding `<root>/~/x`, which passes every containment check and opens as a workspace file tab whose Open-in-editor fails with path_not_found.
r.proposedFix: Add `isHomeRelativePath(path)` (regex /^~[^/]*(?:\/|$)/) and include `isHomeRelativePath(parsedHref.path)` in the early-return guard of resolveRelativeLocalFileHref, next to the startsWith("/") check. It runs on the decoded href so `%7E/` is covered too. Verified in worktree: repro test 5/5 green, existing markdown-local-file-link/markdown-preview tests pass, turbo typecheck @bb/app clean, live app shows plain code / plain anchor. Diff saved at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1182/repro/proposed-fix.diff. Add the tilde cases to markdown-local-file-link.test.ts. Option 2 (expand ~ via host home) would need a new host payload field + HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump and should be a separate change.
r.caveats: Not fixed on origin/main as of today (git log 16ceb3a54..origin/main on the file is empty). PR #1504 was an agent duplicate, already closed; no open PR to review. Sawyer's comment that percent-encoded `%7E/` needs separate handling is inaccurate for a check placed after safeDecodeURIComponent (the natural spot); only double-encoded `%257E` survives, harmlessly. Bare unformatted `~/x` text is not autolinked; the bug requires inline code ending in .md/.markdown or an explicit markdown link, and only in assistant messages (also markdown file previews and plugin panels via the same resolver). After the fix `[t](~/x)` remains a plain relative anchor (dead in-app route on click) rather than being fully de-linked. findings.section: Proposed fix (first principles) — Notes / what could go wrong
findings.problem: The report claims the regex /^~[^/]*(?:\/|$)/ deliberately keeps '~$report.docx' and '~notes.md' as legitimate relative names. That is false: '[^/]*' consumes the whole first segment and '$' then always matches, so the regex is equivalent to /^~/ and rejects every path starting with '~'.
findings.evidence: node /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1182/verify/regex.js prints true for '~notes.md', '~$report.docx', '~notes.md:3', '~foo/bar.md' as well as '~', '~/x', '~user/x.md'.
findings.fix: Either state honestly that the fix rejects any href beginning with '~' (probably acceptable) or change the regex to something like /^~[A-Za-z0-9._-]*(?:\/|$)/ combined with an explicit list, and add '~notes.md' as a positive (still-linkified) test case so the claim is actually verified.

findings.problem: Ports (25374/33374), host id (host_7jfebaa4wr) and project/thread ids are the author's instance values but are given as literal commands; and the scratch-repo line ends with 'cd /tmp/bb-1182-scratch', so the next line 'pnpm bb:dev machine list' fails with ERR_PNPM_NO_IMPORTER_MANIFEST_FOUND when followed literally.

r.rootCauseOneLine: createConnectServerSync.runSync() treats a null fetchServers() (no local runtime + no cached credential, or any RPC/gate failure) as a log-only silent no-op and never informs main.ts, so buildMenuServerItems maps an empty list and createServerMenuItems renders no empty-state row; the distinct reasons (503 disabled vs not_paired vs no credential) are available but discarded by design.

prReviews.verdict: REQUEST CHANGES (reporter's prototype branch Joesirven/bb@prototype/connect-server-list-skip-reason, no PR opened)
prReviews.topFinding: A skipped sync never triggers refreshApplicationMenu(); in the reporter's custom-target startup flow the last menu build (main.ts:1235) precedes connectServerSync.syncNow() (main.ts:2288) which sets the reason, and the remote config poll that would rebuild fails for an unreachable target, so the disabled note would not appear when it is needed. Also 'unavailable' mislabels 503/not_paired as 'could not reach bb Connect' though the server distinguishes them; skipReason set before await; optional+nullable serversNote; no tests.

r.proposedFix: In apps/desktop/src/connect-server-sync.ts make the sync outcome a value: return a discriminated result from fetchServers (no-local-server-no-credential; local-plugin-disabled from RPC 503; local-not-paired from {code:'handler_error',message:'not_paired'}; local-unreachable; gate-unauthorized/gate-unreachable from ConnectListError) by parsing rpcFailureSchema instead of discarding it, and add an onSkipped(reason) callback next to onServers. In main.ts store the reason beside connectAccountServers and call refreshApplicationMenu() from onSkipped too (Electron menus are immutable after build). In menu.ts render a required `serversNote: string | null` as a disabled item only when the connect list is empty and a reason exists, with labels per reason; update the 'stays quiet' test and add a menu test. Optionally add a clickable 'Sign in to bb Connect…' that switches to builtin and opens pairing (product decision). No wire/protocol impact.
r.caveats: No macOS available; the Server submenu was rendered with the real, unmodified menu.ts inside Electron 41.7.0 under Xvfb on Linux with the servers array main.ts produces for the reporter's state (isMac:false; template is platform-independent apart from role items). The prototype's main.ts ordering defect is from reading base main.ts control flow, not from running the prototype app. The reporter's claim that the menu had only 'This Mac' and 'Set Server URL…' is slightly off (a saved custom target also lists the custom host). Reporter's remedy ('sign in to Connect') would additionally require pairing the Mac's local server to the same account, since the desktop credential can only be enrolled via its own local server.

findings.section: Root cause (Mechanism bullet 1) and Prototype review finding #1
findings.problem: The startup control flow described for the reporter's exact scenario is wrong. The report says runDesktopApp runs `await applyServerTarget(); connectServerSync.syncNow()` and that the last menu build is refreshApplicationMenu() at main.ts:1235 before syncNow at 2288 sets the reason. But for an unreachable custom URL, applyServerTarget's `await loadWindowUrl({url: target.url})` (main.ts:1229) rejects (BrowserWindow.loadURL rejects with ERR_FAILED/ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED; loadUrlIntoWindow only swallows ERR_ABORTED), so neither the refresh at 1235, startRemoteSystemConfigSync at 1233, nor syncNow at 2288 ever run; the promise unwinds to the runDesktopApp catch which shows the 'Could not open bb' error screen. The reporter's own #1494 (which the report cites) documents exactly this. The first sync in that scenario happens only when the user opens Window>Server (menu-will-show -> onListRequested, main.ts:757-761). The report's conclusions (silent null, prototype note would not show at first open) still hold — arguably more strongly — but the cited evidence/line ordering is inaccurate and the report states 'high confidence' in it.
findings.evidence: apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1226-1235 (custom branch: bbAppLoaded=true; await loadWindowUrl; startRemoteSystemConfigSync; refreshApplicationMenu), desktop-window-factory.ts:197-210 (rethrows non-ERR_ABORTED), main.ts:2292-2301 (catch -> loadStartupError). Issue #1494 body: 'refreshApplicationMenu() at the end of applyServerTarget() never runs'.
findings.fix: Rewrite the mechanism bullet: in the reporter's flow the startup sync never runs because applyServerTarget rejects; the sync first runs from onServerMenuWillShow while the popup is already built, and a skipped sync never rebuilds the menu. Update the prototype review's cited lines accordingly (menu built at main.ts:2272 / menu-will-show at 757-761 rather than 1235 vs 2288).

findings.problem: The failing assertion in test 1 (`expect(Object.keys(sync)).toContain('getSkipReason')`) asserts the reporter's prototype API name rather than an observable bug; it would still fail against a valid fix that uses a callback (which is what the report's own proposed fix recommends). The bug itself is documented by the passing assertions plus test 2.
